chapters.1.lds: The selected Church lesson connects God's light and love with the conduct described here. Why does honest confession belong within walking in light?
chapters.1.summary: The writer announces what he has heard, seen, and touched: the Word of life. He writes so readers may share fellowship with the Father and the Son. God is light, and in him is no darkness. Anyone who claims fellowship and walks in darkness lies. If we walk in the light, Jesus’ blood cleanses us from all sin. If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves. If we confess our sins, he is faithful to forgive.
chapters.2.lds: The selected Church lesson connects God's light and love with the conduct described here. How does love for a visible brother test a claim about knowing Christ?
chapters.2.summary: The writer says he writes so that they will not sin. If anyone sins, Jesus Christ the righteous is an advocate with the Father. Those who know him keep his commandments. The command to love is both old and new. Whoever hates his brother is in darkness. He writes to children, fathers, and young men. They must not love the world, which is passing away. Antichrists have gone out, and the readers should remain in what they heard.
chapters.3.lds: The selected Church lesson connects God's light and love with the conduct described here. How can shared goods give visible form to love?
chapters.3.summary: The writer marvels that believers are called children of God. When Christ appears, they will be like him. Whoever remains in him does not keep on sinning. The message from the beginning is to love one another. Cain killed his brother, and whoever hates is a murderer. Christ laid down his life, and they should lay down theirs for the brothers. One who has goods and shuts out a needy brother lacks God’s love. God’s command is to believe in his Son and love one another.
chapters.4.lds: The selected Church lesson connects God's light and love with the conduct described here. Why does hatred toward a brother contradict professed love for God?
chapters.4.summary: The writer tells them to test the spirits. Every spirit that confesses Jesus Christ come in the flesh is of God. They should love one another, for love is of God. God showed his love by sending his only Son so that they might live. No one has seen God at any time. If they love one another, God remains in them. God is love, and perfect love casts out fear. We love because he first loved us.
chapters.5.lds: The selected Church lesson connects God's light and love with the conduct described here. How does asking according to God's will shape confidence in prayer?
chapters.5.summary: The writer says whoever believes that Jesus is the Christ is born of God. Loving God means keeping his commandments, and they are not heavy. Faith is the victory that overcomes the world. Jesus Christ came by water and blood, and the Spirit testifies. God has given eternal life, and this life is in his Son. The writer wants believers to know that they have eternal life. They may ask according to God’s will and be heard. He ends by telling the little children to keep themselves from idols.
